claim: The superior colliculus (SC) of the midbrain is a major hub for sensory processing, as it receives organized inputs from visual, auditory, and somatosensory modalities.
source: The superior colliculus (SC) of the midbrain is a major hub for sensory processing, as it receives organized inputs from visual, auditory, and somatosensory modalities (May, 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to May, 2006.

claim: The SC is a laminated structure controlling visuo-spatial orientation and attention.
source: The SC is a laminated structure controlling visuo-spatial orientation and attention (May, 2006; Krauzlis et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to May, 2006 and Krauzlis et al., 2013.

claim: Defective visual processing in the SC has been associated with psychiatric conditions.
source: As such, defective visual processing in the SC has been associated with psychiatric conditions (Mathis et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Mathis et al., 2015.

claim: Visual information reaches the superficial layers of the SC, which are innervated both by retinal ganglion cells (RGCs - the retino-collicular projection) and by layer V neurons of the primary visual cortex V1 (the cortico-collicular projection).
source: Visual information reaches the superficial layers of the SC, which are innervated both by retinal ganglion cells (RGCs - the retino-collicular projection) and by layer V neurons of the primary visual cortex V1 (the cortico-collicular projection).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the anatomy of the visual system.

claim: During development in the mouse, the retino-collicular map forms during the first post-natal week.
source: During development in the mouse, the retino-collicular map forms during the first post-natal week, and is followed by the cortico-collicular map, which develops between P6 and P12 (Triplett et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Triplett et al., 2009.

claim: The cortico-collicular map develops between P6 and P12.
source: During development in the mouse, the retino-collicular map forms during the first post-natal week, and is followed by the cortico-collicular map, which develops between P6 and P12 (Triplett et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Triplett et al., 2009.

claim: Visuotopic maps must be aligned to ensure efficient modulation of the SC's retinal response by V1 inputs.
source: These visuotopic maps must be aligned to ensure efficient modulation of the SC's retinal response by V1 inputs (Zhao et al., 2014; Liang et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Zhao et al., 2014 and Liang et al., 2015.

claim: The formation of the visuotopy is a stochastic process instructed by a balanced contribution of molecular cues and correlated neuronal activity.
source: It has been suggested that the formation of the visuotopy is a stochastic process instructed by a balanced contribution of molecular cues and correlated neuronal activity (Chandrasekaran et al., 2005; Tsigankov and Koulakov, 2006; 2010; Triplett et al., 2009; Ackman and Crair, 2014; Owens et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations.

claim: The basic principles and underlying molecular mechanisms governing the alignment of converging maps have not been fully described.
source: However the basic principles and underlying molecular mechanisms governing the alignment of converging maps have not been fully described.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of knowledge in the field.

claim: In the mouse, EPHA4/A5/A6 receptors are present on projecting RGCs in a low-nasal to high-temporal gradient.
source: In the mouse, EPHA4/A5/A6 receptors are present on projecting RGCs in a low-nasal to high-temporal gradient.
evidence: This is established knowledge about Eph receptor expression patterns.

claim: RGC axons are repelled when their EPHAs contact and are activated by collicular EFNA2/A3/A5, expressed in a low-rostral to high-caudal gradient in the SC.
source: RGC axons are repelled when their EPHAs contact and are activated by collicular EFNA2/A3/A5, expressed in a low-rostral to high-caudal gradient in the SC (Lemke and Reber, 2005; Cang and Feldheim, 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Lemke and Reber, 2005 and Cang and Feldheim, 2013.

claim: Counter-gradients of ligands (EFNA2/A3/A5) and receptors (EPHA3/A4/A7) are also present in the RGCs and the SC respectively.
source: Counter-gradients of ligands (EFNA2/A3/A5) and receptors (EPHA3/A4/A7) are also present in the RGCs and the SC respectively, but their role remains controversial (Feldheim et al., 2010; Triplett and Feldheim, 2012; Suetterlin et al., 2012; Weth et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations.

claim: In V1, gradients of EPHA4/A7, running from high-lateral to low-medial have been observed.
source: In V1, gradients of EPHA4/A7, running from high-lateral to low-medial have also been observed, and evidence from genetic analyses suggests their involvement in the development of cortico-collicular projections (Cang et al., 2005; Wilks et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Cang et al., 2005 and Wilks et al., 2010.

claim: Evidence from genetic analyses suggests EPHA4/A7 involvement in the development of cortico-collicular projections.
source: In V1, gradients of EPHA4/A7, running from high-lateral to low-medial have also been observed, and evidence from genetic analyses suggests their involvement in the development of cortico-collicular projections (Cang et al., 2005; Wilks et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Cang et al., 2005 and Wilks et al., 2010.

claim: The formation of the cortico-collicular map requires retinal input.
source: Moreover, the formation of the cortico-collicular map requires retinal input (Khachab and Bruce, 1999; Triplett et al., 2009), but again, the underlying molecular mechanisms remain elusive.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Khachab and Bruce, 1999 and Triplett et al., 2009.

claim: Immunohistochemical staining confirmed ectopic expression of EFNA3 in somata and proximal axons of Isl2(+) RGCs in postnatal day 1 (P1) and P8 Efna3 homozygous knock-in (Efna3KI/KI) mice compared to wild-type (WT) littermates.
source: Immunohistochemical staining confirmed ectopic expression of EFNA3 in somata and proximal axons of Isl2(+) RGCs in postnatal day 1 (P1) and P8 Efna3 homozygous knock-in (Efna3KI/KI) mice compared to wild-type (WT) littermates (Figure 1A–F) without affecting Isl2 expression at P1 (Figure 1G,H).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunohistochemical data shown in Figure 1A-F.

claim: Ectopic EFNA3 expression does not affect Isl2 expression at P1.
source: Immunohistochemical staining confirmed ectopic expression of EFNA3 in somata and proximal axons of Isl2(+) RGCs in postnatal day 1 (P1) and P8 Efna3 homozygous knock-in (Efna3KI/KI) mice compared to wild-type (WT) littermates (Figure 1A–F) without affecting Isl2 expression at P1 (Figure 1G,H).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunohistochemical data shown in Figure 1G,H.

claim: Efna3KI/KI mice present two intermixed sub-populations of RGCs: Isl2(−) cells, expressing wild-type levels of Efna3, and Isl2(+) cells expressing additional Efna3.
source: Efna3KI/KI mice present two intermixed sub-populations of RGCs: Isl2(−) cells, expressing wild-type levels of Efna3, and Isl2(+) cells expressing additional Efna3 (Figure 1E–F,I–N).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1E-F, I-N.

claim: EFNA3 is observed on RGC axons in vitro.
source: EFNA3 is observed on RGC axons in vitro (Figure 1O,Q').
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1O, Q'.

claim: Ectopic expression of EFNA in Isl2(+) RGCs did not induce perceptible changes in synaptic layers or retinal organization.
source: Ectopic expression of EFNA in Isl2(+) RGCs did not induce perceptible changes in synaptic layers or retinal organization (Figure 2A,B).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2A,B.

claim: Quantitative transcript (mRNA) measurement confirmed a two-fold increase of Efna3 mRNA in nasal, central and temporal Efna3KI/KI mutant retinas when compared to WT littermates.
source: Quantitative transcript (mRNA) measurement on RGC cell bodies, performed and standardized as described previously (Reber et al., 2004; Claudepierre et al., 2008) confirmed a two-fold increase of Efna3 mRNA and normal levels of Efna2/a5 mRNA in nasal, central and temporal Efna3KI/KI mutant retinas when compared to WT littermates (Figure 2C).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative RT-PCR data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Efna3KI/KI mutant retinas show normal levels of Efna2/a5 mRNA when compared to WT littermates.
source: Quantitative transcript (mRNA) measurement on RGC cell bodies, performed and standardized as described previously (Reber et al., 2004; Claudepierre et al., 2008) confirmed a two-fold increase of Efna3 mRNA and normal levels of Efna2/a5 mRNA in nasal, central and temporal Efna3KI/KI mutant retinas when compared to WT littermates (Figure 2C).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative RT-PCR data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Efna3KI/KI and Efna3KI/+ mice show normal linear retino-collicular maps, equivalent to those of WT littermates.
source: Plotting these values in Cartesian coordinates, as described previously (Brown et al., 2000; Reber et al., 2004; Bevins et al., 2011), revealed normal linear retino-collicular maps in Efna3KI/KI and Efna3KI/+ mice, equivalent to those of WT littermates (Figure 3A).
evidence: The claim is supported by mapping data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The size and the layering of the retinal TZs are similar between Efna3KI/KI and WT littermates.
source: Detailed analysis showed that the size and the layering of the retinal TZs are similar between Efna3KI/KI and WT littermates (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: Retrograde labelling confirmed that axons from both Isl2(−) and Isl2(+) RGCs project to the SC.
source: Retrograde labelling confirmed that axons from both Isl2(−) and Isl2(+) RGCs project to the SC (Figure 3B–G).
evidence: The claim is supported by retrograde labelling data shown in Figure 3B-G.

claim: Anterograde focal injections show normal retino-geniculate mapping in Efna3KI/KI similarly to WT littermates.
source: Anterograde focal injections show normal retino-geniculate mapping (Figure 3H–K) and labelling by full-eye fills showed normal retino-collicular/geniculate eye-specific segregation (Figure 3L–Q) in Efna3KI/KI similarly to WT littermates.
evidence: The claim is supported by anterograde labelling data shown in Figure 3H-K.

claim: Labelling by full-eye fills showed normal retino-collicular/geniculate eye-specific segregation in Efna3KI/KI similarly to WT littermates.
source: Anterograde focal injections show normal retino-geniculate mapping (Figure 3H–K) and labelling by full-eye fills showed normal retino-collicular/geniculate eye-specific segregation (Figure 3L–Q) in Efna3KI/KI similarly to WT littermates.
evidence: The claim is supported by full-eye fill data shown in Figure 3L-Q.

claim: A two-fold increase of ectopic retinal Efna3 expression in Isl2(+) RGCs does not disturb the formation of the retino-collicular/geniculate mapping nor eye-specific segregation.
source: These results demonstrated that a two-fold increase of ectopic retinal Efna3 expression in Isl2(+) RGCs does not disturb the formation of the retino-collicular/geniculate mapping nor eye-specific segregation.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the experimental data presented in Figure 3.

claim: Quantitative analyses revealed a remarkable duplication of the cortico-collicular map for single injections along the lateral-medial axis of the V1 in 47% of Efna3KI/KI animals.
source: Quantitative analyses using ImageJ revealed a remarkable duplication of the cortico-collicular map for single injections along the lateral-medial axis of the V1 in 47% of Efna3KI/KI (n = 9/19, Figure 4A, Figure 4—figure supplement 1A, Figure 4—figure supplement 2A) and 43% of Efna3KI/+ (n = 7/16, Figure 4B, Figure 4—figure supplement 1B) animals when compared to WT littermates (n = 9, Figure 4C, Figure 4—figure supplement 1C, Figure 4—figure supplement 2B) demonstrating heterogeneity of the phenotype in Efna3 KI mutants.
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative mapping data shown in Figure 4A and supplements.

claim: Quantitative analyses revealed a remarkable duplication of the cortico-collicular map for single injections along the lateral-medial axis of the V1 in 43% of Efna3KI/+ animals.
source: Quantitative analyses using ImageJ revealed a remarkable duplication of the cortico-collicular map for single injections along the lateral-medial axis of the V1 in 47% of Efna3KI/KI (n = 9/19, Figure 4A, Figure 4—figure supplement 1A, Figure 4—figure supplement 2A) and 43% of Efna3KI/+ (n = 7/16, Figure 4B, Figure 4—figure supplement 1B) animals when compared to WT littermates (n = 9, Figure 4C, Figure 4—figure supplement 1C, Figure 4—figure supplement 2B) demonstrating heterogeneity of the phenotype in Efna3 KI mutants.
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative mapping data shown in Figure 4B and supplements.

claim: In 60% of Efna3KI/KI animals, different types of projections (either single or duplicated) were observed in both colliculi of a given animal.
source: This was not observed in 60% of Efna3KI/KI (n = 3/5) and 57% of Efna3KI/+ (n = 4/7) animals when we traced the cortico-collicular projections in both left and right colliculi (Figure 4D,D').
evidence: The claim is supported by bilateral mapping data shown in Figure 4D, D'.

claim: In 57% of Efna3KI/+ animals, different types of projections (either single or duplicated) were observed in both colliculi of a given animal.
source: This was not observed in 60% of Efna3KI/KI (n = 3/5) and 57% of Efna3KI/+ (n = 4/7) animals when we traced the cortico-collicular projections in both left and right colliculi (Figure 4D,D').
evidence: The claim is supported by bilateral mapping data shown in Figure 4D, D'.

claim: Genetic variation is unlikely to contribute to the map heterogeneity between animals of the same genotype.
source: Therefore, genetic variation is unlikely to contribute to the map heterogeneity between animals of the same genotype.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that the same animal can show different projection types in left and right colliculi.

claim: The heterogeneity is most likely the consequence of a stochastic process of map formation.
source: This heterogeneity is most likely the consequence of a stochastic process of map formation, as suggested previously (Owens et al., 2015).
evidence: This is an inference supported by a citation to Owens et al., 2015.

claim: In Efna3KI/KI animals showing the same type of projections between colliculi (40% of the mice), all of these projections were duplicated.
source: In Efna3KI/KI animals showing the same type of projections between colliculi, (40% of the mice) all of these projections were duplicated whereas in the Efna3KI/+ animals, the remaining 43% presented only single projections in both left and right colliculi, suggesting an effect of the level of Efna3 ectopic expression onto cortico-collicular map duplication.
evidence: This is based on the experimental observations of bilateral projections.

claim: In Efna3KI/+ animals, the remaining 43% presented only single projections in both left and right colliculi.
source: In Efna3KI/KI animals showing the same type of projections between colliculi, (40% of the mice) all of these projections were duplicated whereas in the Efna3KI/+ animals, the remaining 43% presented only single projections in both left and right colliculi, suggesting an effect of the level of Efna3 ectopic expression onto cortico-collicular map duplication.
evidence: This is based on the experimental observations of bilateral projections.

claim: All WT animals tested (n = 4) showed single projections in both colliculi.
source: As expected, all WT animals tested (n = 4) showed single projections in both colliculi (Figure 4D).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: There is a significant two-fold difference in map separation between Efna3KI/KI (ΔSexp median = 13%, n = 9) and Efna3KI/+ (ΔSexp median = 7%, n = 7) animals.
source: This revealed a significant two-fold difference in map separation between Efna3KI/KI (ΔSexp median = 13%, n = 9) and Efna3KI/+ (ΔSexp median = 7%, n = 7) animals, which correlates with the presence of one or two copies of the Isl2-ires-Efna3 allele (Figure 4E).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative analysis shown in Figure 4E.

claim: The map separation correlates with the presence of one or two copies of the Isl2-ires-Efna3 allele.
source: This revealed a significant two-fold difference in map separation between Efna3KI/KI (ΔSexp median = 13%, n = 9) and Efna3KI/+ (ΔSexp median = 7%, n = 7) animals, which correlates with the presence of one or two copies of the Isl2-ires-Efna3 allele (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is an inference based on the correlation between genotype and map separation.

claim: Efna3 ectopic expression in Isl2(+) RGC axons/TZs destabilizes the stochastic process of cortico-collicular mapping, leading to map duplication in Efna3 KI animals.
source: Since Isl2 is not expressed in the cortex (see Figure 5B), these results suggest that Efna3 ectopic expression in Isl2(+) RGC axons/TZs destabilizes the stochastic process of cortico-collicular mapping, leading to map duplication in Efna3 KI animals.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental observations and the fact that Isl2 is not expressed in cortex.

claim: V1 EphA-positive cortical axons sense varying EFNA3 levels on RGCs terminals by direct contact with these terminals in the SC.
source: This in turn implies that V1 EphA-positive cortical axons sense varying EFNA3 levels on RGCs terminals by direct contact with these terminals in the SC (Cang et al., 2005) and anterograde labelling from retina and V1 cortex showed that both cortical and retinal axons terminals overlap in the superficial layers of the SC (Figure 4F) (Phillips et al., 2011; Owens et al., 2015).
evidence: This is an inference supported by citations and data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: Both cortical and retinal axons terminals overlap in the superficial layers of the SC.
source: This in turn implies that V1 EphA-positive cortical axons sense varying EFNA3 levels on RGCs terminals by direct contact with these terminals in the SC (Cang et al., 2005) and anterograde labelling from retina and V1 cortex showed that both cortical and retinal axons terminals overlap in the superficial layers of the SC (Figure 4F) (Phillips et al., 2011; Owens et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by anterograde labelling data shown in Figure 4F and citations.

claim: DiI labelled RGC axons were observed in the SC, as well as a strong collicular EFNA3 staining.
source: DiI labelled RGC axons were observed in the SC, as well as a strong collicular EFNA3 staining (Figure 4—figure supplement 3A–F, Figure 5—figure supplement 1A–D').
evidence: The claim is supported by immunohistochemical data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 3A–F and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A–D'.

claim: No EFNA3 staining on single DiI-labelled RGC axons could be detected in neither Efna3KI/KI nor WT littermates.
source: However, no EFNA3 staining on single DiI-labelled RGC axons could be detected in neither Efna3KI/KI nor WT littermates (Figure 4—figure supplement 3A–F).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunohistochemical data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 3A–F.

claim: EFNA3 immunohistochemistry on P3 Efna3KI/KI and WT optic nerve (ON) longitudinal sections showed the presence of EFNA3 on fibers within the proximal part of the ON in Efna3KI/KI and WT littermates.
source: EFNA3 immunohistochemistry on P3 Efna3KI/KI and WT optic nerve (ON) longitudinal sections (proximal, middle and distal to the optic cup) showed the presence of EFNA3 on fibers within the proximal part of the ON in Efna3KI/KI and WT littermates (Figure 4—figure supplements 4A,A', D,D') but not on the proximal part of Efna3−/− ON (Figure 4—figure supplement 4H).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunohistochemical data shown in Figure 4—figure supplements 4A,A', D,D'.

claim: EFNA3 signal was detected in the middle part of the ON in Efna3KI/KI but not in WT.
source: EFNA3 signal was also detected in the middle part of the ON in Efna3KI/KI but not in WT (Figure 4—figure supplements 4B,B', E,E') and was nearly impossible to discern in the distal part of Efna3KI/KI ON (Figure 4—figure supplements 4C,C', F,F'), indicating that EFNA3 is present on RGC axons.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunohistochemical data shown in Figure 4—figure supplements 4B,B', E,E'.

claim: EFNA3 was nearly impossible to discern in the distal part of Efna3KI/KI ON.
source: EFNA3 signal was also detected in the middle part of the ON in Efna3KI/KI but not in WT (Figure 4—figure supplements 4B,B', E,E') and was nearly impossible to discern in the distal part of Efna3KI/KI ON (Figure 4—figure supplements 4C,C', F,F'), indicating that EFNA3 is present on RGC axons.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunohistochemical data shown in Figure 4—figure supplements 4C,C', F,F'.

claim: EFNA3 is present on RGC axons.
source: EFNA3 signal was also detected in the middle part of the ON in Efna3KI/KI but not in WT (Figure 4—figure supplements 4B,B', E,E') and was nearly impossible to discern in the distal part of Efna3KI/KI ON (Figure 4—figure supplements 4C,C', F,F'), indicating that EFNA3 is present on RGC axons.
evidence: This is an inference based on the immunohistochemical data from the optic nerve.

claim: Co-localization of EFNA3 with NF200 on fibers confirmed that EFNA3 is present on RGC axons.
source: This was further confirmed by co-localization of EFNA3 with NF200 on fibers (Figure 4—figure supplement 4I–J' and Figure 1B–F,O–Q').
evidence: The claim is supported by co-localization data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 4I–J' and Figure 1B–F,O–Q'.

claim: Retrograde labelling confirmed that the cortico-collicular projections originate from layer V neurons in V1 cortex in P14 Efna3KI/KI animals.
source: Retrograde labelling confirmed that the cortico-collicular projections originate from layer V neurons in V1 cortex in P14 Efna3KI/KI animals (Figure 5A).
evidence: The claim is supported by retrograde labelling data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: No bi-cistronic expression of Isl2-ires-Efna3 in either SC or V1 cortex of WT and Efna3KI/KI animals could be detected.
source: No bi-cistronic expression of Isl2-ires-Efna3 in either SC or V1 cortex of WT and Efna3KI/KI animals could be detected (Figure 5B), ruling out any indirect effects of Efna3 ectopic expression.
evidence: The claim is supported by PCR data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Transcript analyses in colliculi and V1 cortices revealed similar levels of Efna2/a3/a5 and Epha4/a7 receptors in Efna3KI/KI compared to WT littermates at P7.
source: Transcript analyses in colliculi and V1 cortices revealed similar levels of Efna2/a3/a5 and Epha4/a7 receptors in Efna3KI/KI compared to WT littermates at P7 (Figure 5C) excluding indirect effects due to local changes of Ephas/Efnas gene expression.
evidence: The claim is supported by transcript analysis data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Similar level of EFNA3 between Efna3KI/KI and WT littermates was confirmed by immunostaining of EFNA3.
source: Similar level of EFNA3 between Efna3KI/KI and WT littermates was further confirmed by immunostaining of EFNA3 (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A–E).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A–E.

claim: If the defective cortico-collicular maps in the Efna3 KI animals were solely due to Efna3 ectopic expression in Isl2(+) RGCs, then inactivation of this ectopic expression should rescue the phenotype and restore a wild-type map.
source: If the defective cortico-collicular maps in the Efna3 KI animals were solely due to Efna3 ectopic expression in Isl2(+) RGCs, then inactivation of this ectopic expression should rescue the phenotype and restore a wild-type map.
evidence: This is a logical hypothesis based on the experimental observations.

claim: Co-expression of EFNA3 ligand and EPHA3 receptor in the same cell leads to their mutual inactivation through cis-masking.
source: Previous work showed that co-expression of EFNA3 ligand and EPHA3 receptor in the same cell leads to their mutual inactivation through cis-masking (Falivelli et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Falivelli et al., 2013.

claim: Immunohistochemical staining confirmed co-expression of EFNA3 and EPHA3 in acutely isolated double heterozygous RGCs.
source: Immunohistochemical staining confirmed co-expression of EFNA3 and EPHA3 in acutely isolated double heterozygous RGCs (Figure 6A).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunohistochemical data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Ectopic expression of the EPHA3 receptor in Isl2(+) RGCs in heterozygous Epha3KI/+ animals results in a duplicated retino-collicular map.
source: Importantly, previous studies demonstrated that ectopic expression of the EPHA3 receptor in Isl2(+) RGCs in heterozygous Epha3KI/+ animals results in a duplicated retino-collicular map (Figure 6—figure supplement 1, Brown et al., 2000).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Brown et al., 2000 and data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: Co-expression of Epha3 and Efna3 in Epha3KI/Efna3KI double-mutant mice reverted the duplications, leading to normal retino- and cortico-collicular maps.
source: Remarkably, co-expression of Epha3 and Efna3 in Epha3KI/Efna3KI double-mutant mice reverted the duplications, leading to normal retino- and cortico-collicular maps (Figure 6B,C).
evidence: The claim is supported by mapping data shown in Figure 6B,C.

claim: The double rescue of both maps indicates that cortico-collicular defects in Efna3 KI animals were caused by ectopic expression of EFNA3 in Isl2(+) RGCs and were restored by concomitant expression of EPHA3.
source: This double rescue of both maps indicates that cortico-collicular defects in Efna3 KI animals were caused by ectopic expression of EFNA3 in Isl2(+) RGCs and were restored by concomitant expression of EPHA3.
evidence: This is an inference based on the rescue experiment results.

claim: The cis-inactivation mechanism was cross-validated by the presence of a normal retino-collicular map in the Efna3KI/Epha3KI double mutant mice, indicating EPHA3 inactivation.
source: The cis-inactivation mechanism was cross-validated by the presence of a normal retino-collicular map in the Efna3KI/Epha3KI double mutant mice, indicating EPHA3 inactivation (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is an inference based on the mapping data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Retinal DiI anterograde tracing revealed no retino-collicular duplications, even in the caudal-most pole of the SC, in Epha3KI/Efna3KI::Epha4+/- and Epha3KI/Efna3KI::Epha4−/− compound mutants.
source: Retinal DiI anterograde tracing revealed no retino-collicular duplications, even in the caudal-most pole of the SC, in Epha3KI/Efna3KI::Epha4+/- and Epha3KI/Efna3KI::Epha4−/− compound mutants, confirming inactivation of EPHA3 and EFNA3 in Isl2(+) RGCs (Figure 6D,E).
evidence: The claim is supported by anterograde tracing data shown in Figure 6D,E.

claim: EPHA3 and EFNA3 ectopic expression in the same RGCs lead to their mutual inactivation.
source: Altogether, these results suggest that EPHA3 and EFNA3 ectopic expression in the same RGCs lead to their mutual inactivation and confirm that cortico-collicular mapping duplications observed in Efna3 KI animals are the consequence of retinal EFNA3 ectopic expression.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the compound mutant experiments.

claim: Cortico-collicular mapping duplications observed in Efna3 KI animals are the consequence of retinal EFNA3 ectopic expression.
source: Altogether, these results suggest that EPHA3 and EFNA3 ectopic expression in the same RGCs lead to their mutual inactivation and confirm that cortico-collicular mapping duplications observed in Efna3 KI animals are the consequence of retinal EFNA3 ectopic expression.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the genetic rescue experiments.

claim: Modestly elevated expression of EFNA3 exclusively in a subset of RGCs disturbed cortico-collicular map alignment in the SC.
source: We showed that modestly elevated expression of EFNA3 exclusively in a subset of RGCs disturbed cortico-collicular map alignment in the SC, pointing to a mechanism where retinal EFNA3 provides positional information to ingrowing V1 cortico-collicular axons.
evidence: This is a summary of the experimental findings.

claim: Retinal EFNA3 provides positional information to ingrowing V1 cortico-collicular axons.
source: We showed that modestly elevated expression of EFNA3 exclusively in a subset of RGCs disturbed cortico-collicular map alignment in the SC, pointing to a mechanism where retinal EFNA3 provides positional information to ingrowing V1 cortico-collicular axons.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental findings.

claim: EPHA3/EFNA3 coexpression in the same cell, including RGCs, abolishes their trans-binding to EFNAs and EPHAs.
source: EPHA3/EFNA3 coexpression in the same cell, including RGCs, abolishes their trans-binding to EFNAs and EPHAs (Connor et al., 1998; Hornberger et al., 1999; Menzel et al., 2001; Carvalho et al., 2006; Falivelli et al., 2013; Klein and Kania, 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations.

claim: Each individual Efna3KI/+ and Epha3KI/+ mutant shows robust visuotopic map abnormalities.
source: The power of this approach resides in the fact that each individual Efna3KI/+ and Epha3KI/+ mutant shows robust visuotopic map abnormalities (Brown et al., 2000; Triplett et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Brown et al., 2000 and Triplett et al., 2009.

claim: The presence of WT retino- and cortico-collicular maps in the Efna3KI/Epha3KI double heterozygous mutants provides compelling evidence that both EFNA3 and EPHA3 were inactivated in Isl2(+) RGCs.
source: The presence of WT retino- and cortico-collicular maps in the Efna3KI/Epha3KI double heterozygous mutants provides compelling evidence that both EFNA3 and EPHA3 were inactivated in Isl2(+) RGCs.
evidence: This is an inference based on the double mutant mapping results.

claim: The results confirm the causal role of retinal EFNA3 ectopic expression on cortico-collicular alignment defects.
source: Although we cannot rule out the occurrence of an altered expression/function of other yet unidentified molecules involved in mapping (e.g., semaphorins, L1) by ectopic EFNA3 expression, our results confirm the causal role of retinal EFNA3 ectopic expression on cortico-collicular alignment defects.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the genetic experiments.

claim: Retinal projections play an instructive role in cortico-collicular map formation.
source: They suggest that retinal projections play an instructive role in cortico-collicular map formation.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental findings.

claim: The heterogeneity of the cortico-collicular phenotype in the Efna3 KI mutants is in accordance with previous data showing a variable penetrance of the retinotopic mapping abnormalities in constitutive or conditional Efnas knock-outs.
source: The heterogeneity of the cortico-collicular phenotype in the Efna3 KI mutants, revealed by a mix of single and duplicated projections, is in accordance with previous data showing a variable penetrance of the retinotopic mapping abnormalities in constitutive or conditional Efnas knock-outs (Feldheim et al., 2000; Cang et al., 2008; Suetterlin and Drescher, 2014; Owens et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations.

claim: Variable penetrance of the mutant phenotype can be explained by the stochastic nature of map formation driven by opposing forces resulting from EPHA signaling and correlated neuronal activity.
source: Such variable penetrance of the mutant phenotype can be explained by the stochastic nature of map formation driven by opposing forces resulting from EPHA signaling, which tends to separate neighboring RGCs through repulsion, and correlated neuronal activity, which tends to reinforce neighboring RGCs projections on adjacent target cells (Cang et al., 2008; Triplett et al., 2009; Owens et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Cang et al., 2008, Triplett et al., 2009, and Owens et al., 2015.

claim: The general pattern of V1 collicular projections is consistent with the involvement of cortical EPHA receptor gradients (high-lateral to low-medial).
source: The general pattern of V1 collicular projections is consistent with the involvement of cortical EPHA receptor gradients (high-lateral to low-medial) (Cang et al., 2005) repelled by low-rostral to high-caudal EFNA gradients of retinal origin in the SC (forward signaling).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Cang et al., 2005.

claim: In the Efna3 KI animals, retinal EFNA3 oscillation in the SC organizes neighbor-neighbor relationships of V1 and RGC TZs locally through repulsion inducing a small distance of map duplication.
source: In the Efna3 KI animals, retinal EFNA3 oscillation in the SC organizes neighbor-neighbor relationships of V1 and RGC TZs locally through repulsion inducing a small distance of map duplication.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental observations.

claim: The model is consistent with a retinal-matching model, suggesting that retinal inputs are required for proper cortico-collicular mapping.
source: Our model is consistent with a retinal-matching model, suggesting that retinal inputs are required for proper cortico-collicular mapping (Khachab and Bruce, 1999; Triplett et al., 2009; Cang and Feldheim, 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Khachab and Bruce, 1999, Triplett et al., 2009, and Cang and Feldheim, 2013.

claim: Retinal inputs carry molecular cues, EFNA3 and likely other retinal EFNAs present at the level of the TZs to provide positional information for ingrowing V1 axons.
source: In our model, retinal inputs carry molecular cues, EFNA3 and likely other retinal EFNAs present at the level of the TZs to provide positional information for ingrowing V1 axons (Figure 9).
evidence: This is the proposed model based on the experimental findings, illustrated in Figure 9.

claim: Transposed retinal EFNAs in the SC instruct cortico-collicular map alignment and act together with correlated neuronal activity pattern shared between RGCs and V1 axons.
source: Altogether, our data suggest that transposed retinal EFNAs in the SC instruct cortico-collicular map alignment and act together with correlated neuronal activity pattern shared between RGCs and V1 axons (Triplett et al., 2009; Cang and Feldheim, 2013).
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental findings, supported by citations.

claim: Triplett and collaborators suggested a gradient-matching model which posits that collicular EFNAs are required for the mapping of somatosensory inputs to the SC.
source: Triplett and collaborators (Triplett et al., 2012) suggested a gradient-matching model which posits that collicular EFNAs are required for the mapping of somatosensory inputs to the SC.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Triplett et al., 2012.

claim: The requirement of SC-produced EFNAs for cortico-collicular mapping is unlikely.
source: In contrast, the requirement of SC-produced EFNAs for cortico-collicular mapping is unlikely.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental observations and previous work.

claim: The presence of non-duplicated retino-collicular maps in both Efna3KI/+ and Efna3KI/KI mutants suggests that retinal EFNA3 does not play a significant role in the formation of this map.
source: The presence of non-duplicated retino-collicular maps in both Efna3KI/+ and Efna3KI/KI mutants, as revealed by DiI tracing, suggests that retinal EFNA3 does not play a significant role in the formation of this map, consistent with previous work on Efna3-null mutants (Pfeiffenberger et al., 2006).
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental observations, supported by a citation to Pfeiffenberger et al., 2006.

claim: EFNAs on RGC axons are activated by collicular EPHAs (reverse signaling), leading to axon repulsion.
source: For example, EFNAs on RGC axons are activated by collicular EPHAs (reverse signaling), leading to axon repulsion (Rashid et al., 2005; Lim et al., 2008; Yoo et al., 2011) or branch inhibition in the SC (Yates et al., 2001).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations.

claim: Retinal EFNAs bind to co-expressed retinal EPHAs in the same RGCs leading to inactivation/masking of the EPHA receptors rendering those axons less sensitive to EFNAs binding in the target tissue.
source: In vitro and in vivo transfection in chick neurons suggested that retinal EFNAs bind to co-expressed retinal EPHAs in the same RGCs leading to inactivation/masking of the EPHA receptors rendering those axons less sensitive to EFNAs binding in the target tissue (Connor et al., 1998; Hornberger et al., 1999; McLaughlin and O'Leary, 1999; Menzel et al., 2001; Yin et al., 2004; Carvalho et al., 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations.

claim: The results indicate that EFNA3 ectopic expression does not inactivate endogenous co-expressed EPHA4/A5/A6 receptors in RGCs.
source: Our results rather indicate that EFNA3 ectopic expression does not inactivate endogenous co-expressed EPHA4/A5/A6 receptors in RGCs.
evidence: This is an inference based on the absence of retino-collicular map duplications.

claim: Specific inactivation of EPHA3 by ectopic EFNA3 was shown, suggesting distinctive interactions in cis between EFNA/EPHA pairs.
source: Nevertheless, we showed specific inactivation of EPHA3 by ectopic EFNA3, suggesting distinctive interactions in cis between EFNA/EPHA pairs as previously observed (Yin et al., 2004; Falivelli et al., 2013; Klein and Kania, 2014).
evidence: This is based on the experimental results, supported by citations.

claim: Conditional ablation revealed that high retinal EFNA5 on nasal RGCs axons prevents temporal RGC axons from targeting the caudal SC through fiber-fiber interaction.
source: Conditional ablation revealed that high retinal EFNA5 on nasal RGCs axons prevents temporal RGC axons from targeting the caudal SC through fiber-fiber interaction (Suetterlin and Drescher, 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Suetterlin and Drescher, 2014.

claim: The results suggest that retinal EFNA3 is not involved in fiber-fiber interaction.
source: In our mice, such a mechanism would have generated a local duplication between Isl2(+) and Isl2(-) RGCs or an extension of the TZs in the SC which was not observed, suggesting that retinal EFNA3 is not involved in fiber-fiber interaction.
evidence: This is an inference based on the absence of expected phenotypes.

claim: The data suggest that retinal EFNA3 and EFNA5 present distinct effects on visuotopic mapping and imply a member-specific role of retinal EFNAs in map formation.
source: Together with recent results (Suetterlin and Drescher, 2014), our data further suggest that retinal EFNA3 and EFNA5 present distinct effects on visuotopic mapping and imply a member-specific role of retinal EFNAs in map formation.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental findings and comparison with previous work.

claim: Retinal EPHA receptors are considered to be functionally interchangeable.
source: This is in contrast with retinal EPHA receptors which are considered to be functionally interchangeable (Reber et al., 2004; Bevins et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Reber et al., 2004 and Bevins et al., 2011.

claim: Previous work modelled the stochastic nature of retino-collicular map formation based on the Koulakov model.
source: Previous work modelled the stochastic nature of retino-collicular map formation based on the Koulakov model (Tsigankov and Koulakov, 2006; 2010; Owens et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Tsigankov and Koulakov, 2006, 2010, and Owens et al., 2015.

claim: The 3-step map alignment model substantially modified and expanded the Koulakov algorithm using measured Efna expression data instead of theoretical values.
source: Here, we have substantially modified and expanded this algorithm using our measured Efna expression data instead of theoretical values and simulated the retino- and cortico-collicular mapping process sequentially.
evidence: This describes the methodological approach taken in the study.

claim: Retinal Efna3 expression alone cannot provide positional information, due to its homogeneous expression profile in WT RGCs.
source: We assumed that retinal Efna3 expression alone cannot provide positional information, due to its homogeneous expression profile in WT RGCs.
evidence: This is an assumption made in the modeling approach.

claim: Other EFNAs or other guidance molecules, either retinal or collicular, must participate in the regulation of map alignment.
source: Therefore other EFNAs or other guidance molecules, either retinal or collicular, must participate in the regulation of map alignment.
evidence: This is an inference based on the modeling assumptions.

claim: Retinal EFNA5 has been recently shown to participate in RGCs fiber-fiber interactions.
source: Retinal EFNA5 has been recently shown to participate in RGCs fiber-fiber interactions (Suetterlin and Drescher, 2014) but a given proportion may contribute to map alignment.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Suetterlin and Drescher, 2014.

claim: The model retained 80% of the retinal EFNA5 level and 100% of retinal EFNA2/A3 levels in the algorithm.
source: We chose to retain 80% of the retinal EFNA5 level and 100% of retinal EFNA2/A3 levels in the algorithm.
evidence: This describes a parameter choice in the modeling approach.

claim: Contribution of endogenous collicular EFNAs to cortico-collicular map alignment seems unlikely as these mediated previous RGCs axons guidance.
source: Moreover, contribution of endogenous collicular EFNAs to cortico-collicular map alignment seems unlikely as these mediated previous RGCs axons guidance (Janes et al., 2005), therefore collicular EFNA levels were not included in the V1 projection step of the model.
evidence: This is an inference based on previous work cited (Janes et al., 2005).

claim: The 3-step map alignment model replicates experimental features of both retino- and cortico-collicular maps observed in WT and Efna3 KI animals.
source: The 3-step map alignment model replicates experimental features of both retino- and cortico-collicular maps observed in WT and Efna3 KI animals.
evidence: This is a summary of the modeling results.

claim: The model validates a stochastic mechanism of retinal-dependent molecular cues, involving EFNA3, providing positional information in the SC for V1 axons which then coordinate with correlated neuronal activity to align visuotopic maps.
source: It validates a stochastic mechanism of retinal-dependent molecular cues, involving EFNA3, providing positional information in the SC for V1 axons which then coordinate with correlated neuronal activity (Triplett et al., 2009) to align visuotopic maps.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the modeling results, supported by a citation.

claim: The percentages of duplicated projections generated by the model were similar to the percentages of experimentally measured duplications for both Efna3KI/KI and Efna3KI/+ animals.
source: The percentages of duplicated projections generated by the model were similar to the percentages of experimentally measured duplications (Figure 4A,B) for both Efna3KI/KI and Efna3KI/+ animals (one sample t-test, Efna3KI/KI, p = 0.17; Efna3KI/+, p = 0.22; Figure 8J).
evidence: The claim is supported by statistical comparison shown in Figure 8J.

claim: This new principle may serve as a general framework for sensory map alignment, where positional information, carried by a leading map, acts together with correlated activity, enabling precise adjustments of subsequent projection alignment.
source: From a functional standpoint, this new principle may serve as a general framework for sensory map alignment, where positional information, carried by a leading map, acts together with correlated activity, enabling precise adjustments of subsequent projection alignment.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the broader implications of the findings.

claim: Graded expression of Efna2 and Efna5 was observed along the nasal-temporal axis of the retina.
source: We observed graded expression of Efna2 and Efna5 along the nasal-temporal axis of the retina, whereas Efna3 is homogeneously expressed in WT animals (Figure 7A,B).
evidence: The claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 7A,B.

claim: Efna3 is homogeneously expressed in WT animals.
source: We observed graded expression of Efna2 and Efna5 along the nasal-temporal axis of the retina, whereas Efna3 is homogeneously expressed in WT animals (Figure 7A,B).
evidence: The claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 7A,B.
